title: Finance Operations Associate
description:
Location: Remote (with quarterly team meetups in London)

Our quarterly socials play a huge part in our workplace culture and working relationships and are compulsory for all HQ members. Transport for these are self-funded, so please consider if this is suitable for you before applying.

Team: HQ / Finance

Type: Full-time (Monday-Friday, 9 am - 5.30 pm)

Summary:

Minerva Virtual Academy (MVA) is the UK’s fastest-growing online school, delivering transformative education to students aged 11–18 across the UK and globally. As we continue our ambitious expansion, MVA is on a mission to reimagine schooling for thousands of children underserved by traditional systems. Recognised by OFSTED and trusted by families and education stakeholders, MVA is leading the way in innovation and accessibility in online learning.

As part of our expanding Finance team, we are seeking a proactive and detail-oriented Finance Operations Associate to support our Finance Manager. This is an exciting opportunity to join a dynamic, purpose-driven organisation at a pivotal time of growth. You’ll play a key role in supporting day-to-day financial operations, ensuring accuracy in transaction processing, reconciliations, and workflow improvements.

MVA offers a dynamic, rewarding, and exciting work environment unlike other schools or educational environments. The role presents a remarkable opportunity for the right candidate to be part of a remote team passionate about leading change in the education sector.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Financial Record Management: Maintain accurate and up-to-date financial records in Xero and internal systems, ensuring data integrity across all platforms.

  • Transaction Processing: Oversee daily accounts payable and receivable activities and monitoring outstanding balances.

  • Account Reconciliations: Assist in performing detailed reconciliations for bank accounts, credit cards, and key balance sheet accounts, resolving discrepancies proactively ahead of year end.

  • Operational Support: Support the wider team by managing internal queries and assisting with varied financial procedures to support peak workloads.

  • Month-End Assistance: Contribute to the month-end close process including preparing journals, calculating deferred revenue and ensuring the completeness of financial data.

  • Process Optimisation: Identify and implement improvements to financial workflows and automation to enhance efficiency and scalability.

  • Audit Support: Gather and prepare documentation for year-end audit processes, ensuring adherence to compliance and safeguarding policies.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Liaise with various departments to provide financial insight and support cross-functional projects as required.

Qualifications & Skills:

  • Part-qualified accountant (AAT, ACCA, CIMA)

  • Solid understanding of bookkeeping principles, accounts payable, and accounts receivable. Experience with deferred revenue management is desirable

  • Strong proficiency with Xero and advanced Google Sheets (pivot tables, formulas, lookups, etc.).

  • Experience working in a fast-paced SME or growing organisation, ideally within the education or tech sectors.

  • Excellent attention to detail and ability to maintain accuracy under pressure.

  • Versatile mindset with the ability to switch between diverse financial tasks and support varied workstreams.

  • Excellent communication skills, capable of collaborating effectively within a remote team.

  • Ability to prioritise workload and meet deadlines in a changing environment.

What We Offer

  • Fully remote working with occasional in-person team sessions in London (four times per year).

  • A supportive, inclusive, and collaborative work culture within a purpose-driven organisation.

  • Opportunities for professional development within a fast-scaling company.

  • Employee well-being initiatives and access to our Employee Assistance Programme (EAP).

Candidate requirements

  • This role offers the freedom to work from wherever you live! We meet up in person four times a year in London, which is a great way to connect with colleagues face-to-face. Travel and accommodation for these meetups are self-funded.

  • As this is a remote role, you will be required to have a suitable home-working set-up which should include a good internet connection. This is the responsibility of all employees. Equipment such as a laptop is provided by MVA

  • All remote employees are required to agree to our policies, including agreeing to cyber security software.

  • MVA is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. Applicants will be required to undergo child protection screening appropriate to the post, including checks with past employers and the Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS). As part of our Safer Recruitment Policy, online searches will also be carried out as part of due diligence checks ahead of any interviews.

What you need to prepare for your application:

Please submit your CV and cover letter as part of your online application.

A CV only tells us so much, so we'd love to hear more about you in your cover letter, to help us understand what drives you and why you'd be the perfect fit for our team.

Specifically, we'd love to hear about:

  • Your 'Why': What draws you to this role, and why does MVA feel like the right fit for your next career step?

  • Your Background: What relevant experience and skills do you bring to this position? We love hearing about the experiences that have shaped how you work!

  • Your Impact: What will you contribute to our HQ team as we continue to grow?

Don't be afraid to let your personality shine through; we value authenticity, initiative, and a genuine enthusiasm for online education!

Notices

  • We reserve the right to close this vacancy early if we receive sufficient applications for the role. Therefore, if you are interested, please submit your application as early as possible.

More about MVA

MVA is an affordable, accessible online independent secondary school that delivers world-class education with a true sense of community. It is the perfect school for modern times - combining smart technology and engaging online resources with one-to-one support, active group learning, and exciting multi-disciplinary projects.

We offer students the flexibility to learn from the comfort of their home, and anywhere in the world, while ensuring they develop the social skills required to live fulfilling lives and succeed in the workplaces of the future. We champion self-sufficiency, collaboration, problem-solving, creative and critical thinking, leadership, and mindfulness.

Our motto - Together We Thrive - is translated into the day-to-day experience of students & staff at the school through our Ways of Being, devised by students for the whole community. We endeavour always to be:

  • Ambitious

  • Aware

  • Considerate

  • Kind

  • Mindful

  • Reflective

  • Responsible

MVA values the diversity of our workforce and welcomes applications from all sectors of the community.

If you require any reasonable adjustments during the application or recruitment process, please get in touch, as we want to make sure everyone has a fair chance to show us what they can bring to MVA.

If you have any questions about this opportunity, please contact us at recruitment@minervavirtual.com.

title: Vi søker ekstrahjelp til Glitter Down Town

  • Sørge for at butikken alltid er inspirerende, ryddig og velfylt

  • Hjelpe kundene med å finne riktige produkter

  • Utføre daglige arbeidsoppgaver knyttet til butikkdrift

Er dette deg? 🙋

  • Du har et sterkt engasjement og stor interesse for mote og trender

  • Du bidrar til et godt arbeidsmiljø og lagfølelse blant kollegene

  • Du er ansvarsfull, fleksibel og har en positiv innstilling

  • Det er en fordel om du har erfaring fra handel, salg eller service

title: IKM -BUSINESS SERVICE PROVIDER
description:
The Mennonite Economic Development Associates (MEDA) invites applications for IKM Business Service Provider to support the implementation of the Project’s annual monitoring and data collection activities, particularly the collection, validation, and documentation of quantitative and qualitative information from RIISA-supported Smallholder Farmers (SHFs), Cooperatives, Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs), and other project clients and partners, as applicable.

BACKGROUND

Mennonite Economic Development Associates (MEDA), with support from the Government of Canada through Global Affairs Canada (GAC), is implementing the Resilience and Inclusion through Investment for Sustainable Agrikultura (RIISA) Project in the Philippines.


The Project works to improve the productivity, income, resilience, and economic participation of cacao smallholder farmers and enterprises, particularly women and other groups that may experience barriers to participation in economic opportunities. RIISA also promotes gender equality and social inclusion, environmentally sustainable and climate-resilient practices, responsible investment, and stronger market systems in communities vulnerable to economic, climate, and conflict-related risks.

RIISA seeks to contribute to improved economic resilience and inclusive economic opportunities among smallholder farmers (SHFs), cooperatives, small and medium enterprises (SMEs), and other market actors in the cacao sector, particularly in Mindanao. The project integrates gender equality and social inclusion, environment and climate change, human rights, market systems development, and gender responsive/environmental, social and governance approaches into its interventions.


The Project will undertake two major Impact and Knowledge Management activities in January to May 2027:


  1. FY6 Annual Survey, which will generate updated evidence on project performance against outcome and selected output indicators; and
  2. Final Evaluation, which will assess the relevance, effectiveness, efficiency, sustainability, impact or emerging impact, gender equality and social inclusion results, environmental performance, and key lessons generated during project implementation.


To ensure these activities are implemented in a timely, systematic, credible, and coordinated manner, MEDA intends to engage an Impact & Knowledge Management Service Provider to partly manage the Annual Survey Data Collection, Processing, Analysis and Narrative Reporting from January to April, as well as lead the process of conducting RIISA Project Final Evaluation from Mid March to early June 2027.


PURPOSE OF ENGAGEMENT

The purpose of this engagement is to provide specialized Impact and Knowledge Management services to ensure the effective planning, coordination, implementation, quality assurance, analysis, documentation, and reporting of the RIISA FY6 Annual Survey and Final Evaluation.


The Service Provider will work closely with the RIISA Impact & Knowledge Management team, Project Management, technical teams, clients, partner organizations, data collectors, and other relevant stakeholders.


The assignment will ensure that project performance evidence is complete, reliable, properly documented, gender-responsive, and suitable for use in MEDA and GAC reporting, project learning, final results documentation, dissemination, and project closeout.

OBJECTIVES


  1. Co-manage the end-to-end implementation of the FY6 Annual Survey, including field preparation, data collection, data quality assurance, processing, analysis, and narrative reporting.
  2. Ensure Annual Survey data are collected and analyzed in accordance with the RIISA Performance Measurement Framework, approved methodologies, indicator definitions, and MEDA data-quality standards.
  3. Coordinate the participation of smallholder farmers, cooperatives, SMEs, financial institutions, project partners, and other relevant respondents in the Annual Survey and Final Evaluation.
  4. Provide technical and logistical coordination for the RIISA Final Evaluation, including preparation of documents, datasets, stakeholder schedules, consultations, field visits, and validation activities.
  5. Lead the Final Evaluation team in accessing complete, organized, and reliable project data and evidence.
  6. Facilitate coordination among MEDA, project partners, beneficiaries, service providers, and the evaluation team throughout the Final Evaluation process.
  7. Support the review and quality assurance of preliminary and final evaluation findings to ensure consistency with available project evidence while maintaining evaluator independence.
  8. Consolidate learning evidences gained from Annual Survey and Final Evaluation for use in final project results reporting, production of knowledge products, end-of-project results dissemination, and project closeout. Support the review and quality assurance of preliminary and final evaluation findings to ensure consistency with available project evidence while maintaining evaluator independence.
  9. Consolidate project monitoring, survey, evaluation, and learning evidence for use in final project reporting, knowledge products, results dissemination, and project closeout

KEY DELIVERABLES and INDICATIVE SCHEDULE


Inception meeting - December 2026

  1. Review of finalized Annual Survey tools, survey protocols, respondent/sample lists, field implementation plan, training materials, and digital survey setup - January 2027
  2. Enumerator/field-team training completed and documented - January 2027
  3. Management and supervision of Annual Survey data collection activities, including regular progress and data-quality reports- January to March 2027
  4. Finalized and cleaned Annual Survey dataset, data-quality documentation, coding documentation, and preliminary indicator tables- February to March 2027
  5. Annual Survey analysis, indicator calculations, comparative analysis, and draft Annual Survey Results Report - March to April 2027
  6. Final Evaluation evidence repository/document index, stakeholder list, evaluation coordination plan, and fieldwork schedule - March 2027
  7. Final Evaluation stakeholder scheduling, and provision of logistical support. data collection, data/evidence provision, data processing and analysis - March to May 2027
  8. Final Evaluation Results Report, cleaned datasets, analysis files, and presentation of key findings - May 2027
  9. Support to evaluation validation, factual review, consolidation of MEDA comments, and management response preparation- May 2027
  10. Consolidated final project results dataset and evidence package for use in the Final Project Results Report and project closeout - May 2027
  11. Completion Report summarizing activities completed, outputs delivered, outstanding evaluation actions, lessons learned, and recommendations- June 4, 2027


EXPECTED OUTPUTS

By the end of the engagement, the Service Provider is expected to have produced or supported completion of the following:


  1. Annual Survey data processing, analysis and Annual Survey Results report preparation and narrative writing;
  2. Final Evaluation data-collection tools;
  3. Final Evaluation Enumerator training materials and training documentation;
  4. Final Evaluation respondent sampling and data-collection tracking system;
  5. Data-quality monitoring reports;
  6. Cleaned and validated Annual Survey and Final Evaluation datasets;
  7. Indicator calculation sheets and analysis tables;
  8. Final Evaluation evidence repository and document inventory;
  9. Final Evaluation stakeholder and consultation schedule;
  10. Evaluation coordination and progress documentation;
  11. Consolidated MEDA comments/factual reviews of draft evaluation outputs;
  12. Key findings and learning summaries;
  13. Organized archive of Annual Survey and Final evaluation materials; and
  14. End-of-engagement Completion Report.


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND COMPETENCIES

The Service Provider may be an individual consultant, consulting team, firm, research institution, or other qualified service provider possessing the necessary technical and operational capacity.



The Service Provider and its team, if applicable, should demonstrate:


Advanced university degree or equivalent professional experience in Monitoring and Evaluation, Development Studies, Economics, Statistics, Social Sciences, Agriculture, International Development, Knowledge Management, or a related field.

  • At least
    five (5) years of relevant professional experience in monitoring, evaluation, survey management, research, impact measurement, or knowledge management.
  • Demonstrated experience managing large-scale quantitative and/or mixed-method surveys.
  • Demonstrated experience in evaluation management, evaluation coordination, or supporting independent evaluations.
  • Strong understanding of results-based management and performance measurement frameworks.
  • Experience in data management, quality assurance, analysis, interpretation, and reporting.
  • Proficiency in Excel and data-management platforms such as KoboToolbox or equivalent survey software as well as visualization apps such as PowerBi and CANVA.
  • Experience in analyzing disaggregated data, including sex-, age-, and other inclusion-related variables.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of gender equality, social inclusion, environment and climate change, and inclusive economic development approaches.
  • Strong technical writing and analytical skills.
  • Ability to communicate complex data and findings in clear and accessible formats.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple workstreams and meet strict deadlines.
  • Demonstrate adaptive capacity, flexibility and must be responsiveness as required by the engagement.
  • Strong facilitation, coordination, and stakeholder-management skills

Experience with Global Affairs Canada-funded projects, agriculture/value-chain development, market systems development, SMEs, cooperatives, financial institutions, or Mindanao-based development programs will be considered an advantage.


Where the engagement is undertaken by a firm or team, MEDA may require the proposed team to include, at minimum:

  • Team Lead / Senior Impact & Evaluation Specialist
  • Survey/Data Management Specialist
  • Field Data Collectors, as required


PROPOSAL SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS

  • Technical proposal describing the proposed approach and methodology;
  • Detailed workplan for January–June 2027;
  • Proposed team composition and roles;
  • Curriculum vitae of key personnel;
  • Evidence of similar assignments;
  • At least two professional references;
  • Financial proposal showing professional fees and other anticipated costs;
  • Proposed level of effort by team member;
  • Declaration of any actual or potential conflict of interest; and
  • Other organizational, registration, tax, or procurement documents required by MEDA.


APPLICATION DEADLINE: 5 November 2026

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis when received. All employment decisions are made on the basis of qualifications and organizational needs. Only successful applicants will be contacted.


MEDA welcomes and encourages applications from all genders, backgrounds, religions, cultures, nationalities and abilities. Accommodation is available on request for candidates with disabilities taking part in the selection process.

title: Youth Employment Specialist
description:
Job Summary

The Youth Employment Specialist works to increase the income of young people enrolled in Youth Pathways South LA while they are in the program. The position connects participants to part-time work, early employment, internships and apprenticeships, helps them apply, prepare and get hired, and stays with them through the first months on the job so that the placement holds. The Youth Employment Specialist works with the Career Coach on the career pathways identified for each youth and works closely with the case managers and the Youth Pathways Lead to remove the barriers that stand between a young person and a paycheck.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Key Areas of Responsibility:

  • Increase participant income during program participation through part-time and early employment, paid work experience, internships, apprenticeships, benefits enrollment and other sources of income.
  • Bridge the gap between youth readiness and the job market, supporting participants through the application, placement and retention process.
  • Work with the Career Coach to move each participant along the career pathway identified for them, and with the case managers and Youth Pathways Lead to remove barriers to employment.

Essential Duties:

  • Work with each participant to build a simple, current picture of their income, including wages, benefits, stipends and other supports, and set an income goal that is reviewed and updated throughout the program.
  • Arrange and coordinate transportation to interviews, orientations, first shifts and work-related appointments, including bus passes, ride share and staff transport where appropriate.
  • Participate in case conferencing with the Youth Pathways Lead, case managers, Career Coach and instructor to review participant progress and coordinate employment goals with the rest of the service plan.
  • Maintain timely and accurate records of employment activity, placements, wages, hours and retention in Salesforce, and provide the Program Manager with regular reporting against grant employment targets.

Other duties and responsibilities may be assigned. The duties and responsibilities listed are designed to provide typical examples of the work performed; not all duties and responsibilities assigned are included here, nor is it expected that all similar positions will be assigned every duty and responsibility.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities:

  • The ability to communicate with and relate to a diverse group of people including clients, community, employers and other staff.
  • Practical knowledge of the entry-level labor market in Los Angeles, including which employers hire young people quickly, what those jobs pay and what they require.
  • Ability to hold a young person accountable while keeping the relationship intact, using a trauma-informed and strength-based approach.
  • Ability to speak fluent Spanish and English language is preferred.

Experience:

  • 2+ years of experience in employment services, job placement, workforce development, staffing or a closely related field, preferably serving youth or young adults.
  • Experience and/or a strong interest in working with justice-involved youth, youth experiencing homelessness, or opportunity youth.

Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in social work, human services or a related field. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.

Direct Reports:

This position has no direct supervisory responsibilities.

Computer Skills:

  • Experience with Salesforce, Clarity/HMIS or a comparable client data system
  • Proficiency in MS Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook)
  • Ability to use widely supported internet browsers.

Certificates, Licenses and Registrations:

  • None

Travel Requirements:

  • Access to reliable transportation.

Work Environment:

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

Physical Demands:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to stand, sit, walk, stoop, talk, hear, reach above and below shoulders; use hand and finger dexterity, keyboarding and making and receiving telephone calls. The employee may be required on occasion to lift and or carry up to 20 lbs.

Employment with St. Joseph Center is contingent on completion of satisfactory background check.

The position requires an ability to work flexible hours including some early morning, evenings. A bilingual/bicultural background is a plus. Excellent Benefits package available.

title: HR Associate
description:
At Get Licensed, we help people get trained, get licensed and find work, and we do this by leveraging technology to make the whole process as efficient and easy as possible. We operate across a number of verticals, and we’re looking to expand those verticals to cater to demand in the UK. We've helped more than 400,000 people get licensed and find work and are consistently rated 5-star on Trustpilot with over 32,000 reviews.


Get Licensed is a fast-paced technology business at heart (the majority of our team are developers or tech wizards), and we are at an exciting stage of our business, having tripled since 2020. We have ambitious plans to significantly scale our existing business, broaden our product suite, and continue to grow profitably revenue year on year, with a clear roadmap of how we will get there.


About the Role

We’re looking for a tech-savvy, people-focused HR Associate to join our People & Culture team. Working closely with the HR Business Partner, you will support HR operations, performance management, employee development, and employee services. You will also use HR systems, data, and company-approved AI tools to improve reporting, simplify everyday processes, and deliver a better employee experience. This role is suited to someone who combines strong HR fundamentals with digital confidence, attention to detail, and a proactive approach to getting things done.


What you will be doing:

HR Operations & Compliance

  • Support the HRBP in managing day-to-day HR operations and projects.
  • Maintain accurate employee records, HR databases, and documentation, including contracts, letters, and policy documents.
  • Support compliance audits and help ensure HR processes align with company policies, applicable labour laws, and HR best practices.
  • Coordinate with Finance on payroll-related administrative tasks.

Performance Management & Training Support

  • Coordinate performance management activities, including goal setting, monthly review meetings, feedback sessions, and mid-year and annual reviews.
  • Collaborate with internal teams to identify training needs and organise internal and external learning sessions.
  • Maintain training trackers, collect feedback, and track progress across employee development programmes..

Onboarding, Offboarding & Employee Services

  • Coordinate employee lifecycle activities, including onboarding, offboarding, documentation, and induction scheduling.
  • Serve as a point of contact for employee queries related to HR policies, health insurance, and OPD benefits.
  • Track insurance claims (OPD & IPD) and coordinate with relevant vendors and providers to support timely resolution.

HR Systems, Analytics & Reporting

  • Maintain accurate employee data in BambooHR and MiHCM, and support routine system updates and workflows.
  • Prepare and update HR reports, dashboards, and presentations covering employee data, attrition, performance, and engagement.
  • Review data for accuracy and completeness, and highlight trends or discrepancies for follow-up.

Employee Engagement & Process Improvement

  • Support initiatives focused on employee engagement, workplace culture, and retention.
  • Identify repetitive administrative tasks and contribute to practical improvements through digital tools and workflow automation.
  • Use company-approved AI tools to support research, drafting, and routine tasks, while checking output accuracy and protecting employee confidentiality.


What we are looking for:

A tech-savvy, people-focused HR professional who enjoys using data, digital tools, and smarter processes to improve the employee experience.

  • Education: A bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Management Sciences, Business Analytics, or a related field.
  • Relevant experience: 1–3 years of experience in HR operations or a generalist role, preferably within a technology-driven or fast-paced organisation.
  • HR fundamentals: A sound understanding of employee lifecycle management, employee relations, performance management, and learning and development.
  • Digital confidence: Hands-on experience with HRIS or digital people platforms, and the ability to learn new tools quickly. Familiarity with BambooHR or MiHCM is an advantage.
  • Data and reporting skills: Strong working knowledge of Excel or Google Sheets, including formulas, lookup functions, pivot tables, and data validation. Ability to turn employee data into clear reports and useful insights.
  • AI and automation awareness: Practical familiarity with tools such as ChatGPT or Claude, including when and how to use them responsibly. Exposure to no-code automation or dashboarding tools is a plus.
  • Communication and ownership: Strong written and verbal communication skills, attention to detail, and the ability to coordinate across teams, manage priorities, and follow through independently.
  • Curiosity and integrity: A willingness to learn, improve existing processes, and collaborate with others while handling sensitive employee information professionally.


Expected Behaviours

We work in an open, collaborative environment where colleagues are encouraged to take responsibility, contribute ideas, and get involved from day one. Above all, we expect everyone at Get Licensed to Do the Right Thing.


Our behaviors guide how we work and form part of our monthly performance reviews:

  • Agility: We move fast, adapt quickly, and continuously improve.
  • Curiosity: We never stop learning and seeking better ways to do things.
  • Excellence: We set new standards and strive to exceed expectations.
  • Love: We care deeply for the work we do, for each other, and for our customers.
  • Ownership: Take responsibility, be accountable, own your mistakes.


What we offer:

  • Competitive compensation, private medical insurance, and paid annual leave.
  • Opportunities for professional development and career growth within People & Culture.
  • Hands-on exposure to HR technology, people analytics, and process improvement projects.
  • The opportunity to contribute to employee learning, engagement, and the wider employee experience.
  • A collaborative team where ideas are welcomed, ownership is encouraged, and contributions are recognised.


Ready to combine your HR knowledge with a smarter, more digital approach to work? Apply to join our People & Culture team.

  • We are Family: We work together as a supportive, caring community, creating a sense of belonging and strength.

Joining Upbring means becoming part of a family of passionate individuals who are fearless in their pursuit of lasting change. Together, we are making a difference, one life at a time.

Your Mission in Action

The Program Assistant provides support for the Neighborhood House program and Director of Emergency Assistance, which includes, but is not limited to, handling all inquiries for services, scheduling appointments for utility assistance, processing and reviewing applications, and processing utility payments and food vouchers in accordance with Agency and licensing standards and other federal, state, and local regulatory requirements on an as-needed basis.

Responsibilities

  • Schedule appointments for utility assistance
  • Review applications and ensure all forms and attachments are properly and accurately completed, signed, and dated
  • Assist applicants in completing applications for utility assistance and food vouchers
  • Assist with preparing reports for the utility grant and food vouchers as requested
  • Analyze, process and approve food vouchers under program policy guidelines
  • Serve as a contact for all inquiries related to program information related to utility assistance and food vouchers
  • Ensure client and sensitive Agency information, files, and records are securely maintained
  • Maintain the confidentiality of all client and Agency information
  • Assist the Director with reviewing and printing client utility bills, calculating the amount the agency can pledge toward the outstanding balance, and determining the appropriate multi-payment amount based on the program guidelines and available funding
  • Assist the Director with reviewing and processing utility payments, financial-related invoices, and statements, and follow up as needed
  • Assist with the preparation and submission of reports to funding sources, the local advisory committee, and applicable departments within Upbring
  • Work closely with the Director of Emergency Assistance and program staff to ensure the program is operating effectively and efficiently, and meeting the needs of the clients and operating in accordance to Agency and licensing standards, funding requirements, and other federal, state, and local regulatory requirements
  • Work as team player and exhibit professional behavior and a positive attitude with both internal and external clients that reflects positively on the Agency and is consistent with Agency policies and practices

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

  • High School Diploma or equivalent
  • Two (2) years of clerical or administrative experience
  • Ability to build a positive rapport with people, strong customer service skills
  • Strong people and interpersonal skills with the demonstrated ability to communicate professionally, interact with all levels of management in a clear and concise manner
  • Ability to work independently with limited supervision; ability to take initiative
  • Ability to work with different programs with different requirements simultaneously including making decisions
  • Strong computer skills; high proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, and Outlook

Preferred Qualifications

  • Associate's degree in Business Administration or closely related field
  • Three (3) years of clerical or administrative experience
  • Bilingual (fluent in Spanish written and conversational), highly preferred

Physical Demands & Work Conditions
  • This position requires sitting and looking and using a computer for long periods of time
  • Position requires frequent standing and walking
  • Lift, push, pull, move up to 25 lbs
The physical requirements for this position with or without reasonable accommodation are representative of those that must be met by an employee to perform the essential functions of this position successfully. While performing this position the employee with or without reasonable accommodation should have the ability to walk, stand, sit, kneel, speak, and hear with aid, see, read, reach with arms and hands, lift and/or move up to specified weight, and use equipment that is essential to performing the job, such as a computer, copier, fax machine, telephone, and automobile, if applicable. Specific vision requirements of this position may include color vision, seeing things close up, and the ability to adjust focus.

title: Vyresnysis (-ioji) informacijos vadybininkas (-ė)
description:
Ar tau patinka dalytis žiniomis, kurti informatyvų turinį ir organizuoti veiklas, kurios skatina smalsumą? KTU Bibliotekoje galėsi prisidėti prie to, kad studentams, tyrėjams ir visai Universiteto bendruomenei būtų lengva atrasti bibliotekos paslaugas, naudotis jos ištekliais ir atrasti naujų mokymosi galimybių. Jei mėgsti derinti komunikaciją, darbą su žmonėmis ir renginių organizavimą – kviečiame prisijungti prie komandos!

Tavo misija:

  • rengti, skelbti ir atnaujinti informaciją bibliotekos tinklalapyje bei socialiniuose tinkluose;

  • kurti informacinę medžiagą apie bibliotekos paslaugas ir išteklius, konsultuoti kolegas jos rengimo klausimais;

  • organizuoti individualius ir grupinius vartotojų mokymus bei pristatymus, rengti mokymo medžiagą;

  • organizuoti švietėjiškus ir kultūrinius renginius bei parodas, rūpintis jų įgyvendinimu ir sklaida;

  • vesti pažintines ekskursijas, supažindinti lankytojus su biblioteka, jos ištekliais, paslaugomis ir naudojimosi jais tvarka.

Ko tikimės iš tavęs?

  • aukštojo universitetinio išsilavinimo;

  • puikių lietuvių kalbos ir gerų anglų kalbos žinių (ne žemesniu nei B2 lygiu);

  • gebėjimo organizuoti renginius ir mokymus;

  • gerų konsultavimo ir klientų aptarnavimo įgūdžių, gebėjimo aiškiai perteikti informaciją;

  • labai gerų darbo kompiuteriu įgūdžių;

  • gebėjimo dirbti savarankiškai ir komandoje.

Būtų puiku, jei :

  • tavo išsilavinimas būtų susijęs su informacijos paslaugų kryptimi;

  • turėtum informacijos ir komunikacijos mokslų žinių;

  • turėtum viešojo kalbėjimo ir mokymų vedimo patirties.

Siūlome:

  • prasmingą darbą KTU – viename didžiausių technologiškųjų universitetų Baltijos šalyse ir lyderiaujančioje aukštojoje mokykloje Lietuvoje;

  • profesionalią ir palaikančią komandą, orientuotą į kokybę, bendradarbiavimą ir rezultatą;

  • įtraukią darbo aplinką, kurioje puoselėjama pagarba, užtikrinamos lygios galimybės ir vertinama įvairovė;

  • galimybę tobulinti profesines kompetencijas: vidinius ir išorinius mokymus, tarptautinius seminarus, stažuotes;

  • gerovės sprendimus: partnerių nuolaidas su „Perks“, darbuotojų gerovės programą „Kaip tu“, papildomą sveikatos draudimą, papildomas atostogų dienas, galimybę naudotis treniruoklių salėmis;

  • aktyvų bendruomenės gyvenimą: darbuotojų renginius ir veiklas, stiprinančias tarpusavio ryšius;

  • atlyginimą nuo 1965 iki 2162 Eur bruto, priklausomai nuo tavo patirties ir kompetencijų.

Ar KTU kitas tavo karjeros žingsnis?

Jei jauti, kad šis darbo pasiūlymas atitinka tavo vertybes ir profesinius tikslus – kviečiame kandidatuoti!

Už kiekvienos technologijos – žmogus. Už sklandžios KTU Bibliotekos veiklos – TU.

title: HR Co-ordinator
description:
Love HR? Curious about people, employment law and what makes businesses tick? This could be the role you've been looking for.

We're looking for a bright, enthusiastic and resourceful HR Co-ordinator to join our HR team at Cintra HR & Payroll Services in our Milton Keynes office.

But let's be clear from the outset, this isn't your typical HR administration role!

Yes, there will be some administration (it's HR, after all!), but this is a role with real variety, genuine responsibility and plenty of opportunities to develop your knowledge and skills.

One day you might be supporting a recruitment campaign, interviewing candidates or working with a hiring manager. The next, you could be researching an employment law question, helping a client implement new HR policies, undertaking a salary benchmarking exercise or coordinating an important HR project.

You'll work closely with our experienced HR Advisers, HR Administration team and Director of HR, gaining exposure to a fascinating range of businesses, industries and people challenges.

If you're someone who loves learning, enjoys solving problems and gets real satisfaction from doing things properly, we'd love to hear from you.

No two weeks are likely to look quite the same, but your responsibilities will include:
  • Getting involved in recruitment: From creating compelling job adverts and screening candidates to working with hiring managers and coordinating onboarding.
  • Supporting real HR projects: Helping deliver initiatives for both Cintra and our clients, including policy implementation, salary benchmarking and workplace risk assessments.
  • Putting your HR knowledge to work: Researching employment law and HR best practice, supporting our HR Advisers and helping develop accurate, practical HR documentation.
  • Working directly with clients: Coordinating onboarding activities, supporting policy implementation and helping clients access the HR services and resources they need.
  • Making things better: Taking ownership of our HR document register, keeping resources accurate and up to date, and spotting opportunities to improve the way we work.
  • Helping us share our expertise: Coordinating client communications, webinars and training activities that keep businesses informed and supported.
And, because we're a busy and evolving HR function, there will undoubtedly be other interesting things to get involved in along the way!
We're less interested in someone who can simply tick boxes and more interested in how you think, how you work and what motivates you.

You'll probably recognise yourself in the following:
  • You're genuinely interested in HR. Not just the processes, but the people, the legislation, the challenges and the thinking behind good HR practice.
  • You're bright and curious. You ask good questions, enjoy researching things and want to understand the why, not just the what.
  • You're resourceful. When faced with something unfamiliar, your instinct is to investigate, think it through and find a sensible way forward.
  • You've got a great eye for detail. Accuracy matters to you. You take pride in producing work that's well thought through, clearly written and right first time.
  • You're a confident communicator. You can write well, speak professionally and build positive relationships with colleagues and clients.
  • You're organised and dependable. You can juggle different priorities, meet deadlines and take ownership of your work.
  • You've got initiative. You don't need to be told every little thing to do — you're comfortable taking responsibility, while knowing when to ask for guidance.
  • You're keen to develop. You see this as an opportunity to build a rewarding career in HR, not simply as your next job.
What experience and qualifications will you need?

We're looking for someone with an CIPD Level 5 qualification (or higher), perhaps even an HR degree, together with a sound understanding of UK employment law fundamentals.

You'll need strong written and verbal communication skills and be comfortable using Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint.

Previous experience in an HR environment would certainly be useful, but we're equally interested in someone at an earlier stage of their career who has the right knowledge, aptitude, attitude and enthusiasm.

We can help you develop your experience. What we can't teach is genuine curiosity, initiative and pride in your work.




At Cintra, our HR team supports businesses across a wide variety of sectors, providing practical, professional and commercially sensible HR advice and support.

That means you'll gain exposure to far more than you might in a traditional in-house HR role.

You'll be surrounded by knowledgeable, approachable colleagues who enjoy what they do and are happy to share their expertise.

You'll be trusted to take ownership of your work, encouraged to contribute ideas and given opportunities to stretch yourself as your confidence and experience grow.

And importantly, there's a genuine career pathway here, with opportunities to progress into HR Advisory and Employee Relations roles as your skills develop.

Our current HR Co-ordinator has thoroughly enjoyed the variety, responsibility and opportunities the role has offered, and we're looking for someone equally enthusiastic to make it their own.

Sound like you?

If you're looking for a role where you can use your brain, develop your HR expertise, make a real contribution and work with a team who genuinely care about what they do, we'd love to hear from you.

Bring us your curiosity, your attention to detail and your enthusiasm for HR. We'll provide the opportunities to put them to good use.

Further details of the role can be found linked in the Job Description. Please note that we do not accept unsolicited CVs from agencies for this position, we thank you for your cooperation. We reserve the right to close this job advert at anytime should there be a high volume of applications.

title: Customer Resolution Associate
description:
About Waystone

Waystone is a leading asset-servicing solutions provider of institutional governance, administration, risk and compliance services to financial institutions. With over 25 years’ experience and a comprehensive range of specialist services to its name, Waystone helps our clients structure, operate and grow through our expertise, innovation and digitisation, backed by the operational scale to support global expansion.\



Summary: Reporting to the Customer Experience & Distributor Support Manager, the Customer Resolution Associate will provide exceptional customer service and technical expertise, particularly when dealing with complaints and expressions of dissatisfaction and effectively handle referrals from colleagues.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

The role of the Customer Resolution Associate will be based within the Leeds Customer Resolution team and dedicated to supporting the business in providing service excellence to Transfer Agency Clients.

A key aspect of this role is to ensure the Customer Resolution team deliver and maintain high quality, accurate and outstanding customer service to the business, client and shareholder always.

The role will support the day-to-day technical referrals within the team and contribute to the daily resource management of cases, ensuring the team provide quality complaint resolutions whilst meeting/exceeding service levels.

The role holder should have a strong understanding of our business, the industry and be experienced in handling complaints and be able to act as a subject matter expert between operational areas and compliance.

They will support the broader Transfer Agency teams and aid their own Manager and the Leadership team.

Demonstrate a keen eye for detail and ability to review and feedback on all aspects of the teams’ work

REQUIREMENTS


Strategic Focus

  • Effectively handle and resolve customer dissatisfaction through all channels and in line with SLAs and industry regulation
  • Encourage and demonstrate active first contact resolution of queries and complaints
  • Advocate correct role model behaviours in terms of speedy and accurate customer resolution via the appropriate channels
  • Ensure complaint processes and procedures are kept up to date
  • Act as a central referral point for CSC colleagues
  • Provide support to the leadership teams as required across Transfer Agency
  • Ensure all teams are accountable and respond in a timely manner to customer queries and complaints

Governance & Risk

  • Technical knowledge in a Financial Services / Funds industry
  • Good understanding of when / how to acknowledge complaints
  • Good understanding of how / when to identify breaches and incidents
  • Working towards (demonstrating an appetite to work towards) IOC qualifications

Experience and Personal Attributes

  • Excellent and proven customer service skills in a Financial Services environment
  • Up to date financial services industry awareness and understanding
  • Experience in the delivery of feedback
  • Ability to act as a coach and mentor to less experienced colleagues
  • Influence internal and external stakeholders and clients
  • Strong interpersonal skills
  • Excellent team working and collaboration
  • IOC modules is desirable but not required

title: Patient Service Specialist
description:
Overview

Are you ready to take your career to new heights? At Concentra, you will be a vital member of our patient care team and play a crucial role in providing exceptional care to our patients. Our mission is to improve the health of America's workforce, one patient at a time. Join us at Concentra and see how your clinical competency and compassion can make a meaningful difference in the lives of the patients you serve.

The Patient Service Specialist performs complex administrative duties including but not limited to patient registration, patient scheduling, providing excellent customer service to clients, and management of multi-line phone system. This role requires a general knowledge of various systems and/or procedures. This position ensures that every patient is treated with quality clinical care and is provided a welcoming and respectful experience.

Responsibilities

  • Greet patients and visitors
  • Communicate wait times to patients and direct them accordingly
  • Obtain authorization, as needed, to process patients for services
  • Check in patients using appropriate patient management system
  • Explain all required forms to patients and ensure proper completion of all paperwork
  • Answer incoming telephone lines and direct the caller accordingly
  • Contact patients regarding appointment reminders, rescheduling, or cancellations.
  • Check out patients in appropriate patient management system and distribute records
  • File paperwork, medical records, and correspondence
  • Maintain inventory of office supplies and printed forms
  • Manage dissemination of all paperwork to outside parties including non-injury, custody, and control forms
  • Follow HIPAA guidelines and safety rules
  • Attend center staff meetings
  • Participate in initial and ongoing training as required
  • Complete processing of patient referrals including accurate checkout, paperwork processing, patient education, and communication with Client Support Group
  • Assist Center Operations Director or other leader in managing daily administrative functions
  • Assist in maintaining a neat, clean, and orderly appearance throughout the facility
  • Use employer reporting tool to scan and distribute employer results and paperwork
  • Review clinician transcriptions and enter applicable charges via internal charge entry system.
  • Perform some medical assistant duties such as breath alcohol tests, drug screens, TB skin test reads and/or other duties as assigned/approved by medical leadership

This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Qualifications

Education Level: High School Diploma or GED

Job-Related Experience

  • 6 months to 1 year
  • Working knowledge of state-specific occupational medicine requirements preferred

Job-Related Skills/Competencies

  • Concentra Core Competencies of Service Mentality, Attention to Detail, Sense of Urgency, Initiative and Flexibility
  • Ability to make decisions or solve problems by using logic to identify key facts, explore alternatives, and propose quality solutions
  • Outstanding customer service skills as well as the ability to deal with people in a manner which shows tact and professionalism
  • The ability to properly handle sensitive and confidential information (including HIPAA and PHI) in accordance with federal and state laws and company policies
  • Demonstrated effective communication and interaction with employers, patients, providers, and other employees
  • Demonstrated ability to maintain working relationship with all levels of employees
  • Demonstrated excellent customer service skills
  • Demonstrated intermediate knowledge of Microsoft Office such as Word, Excel, Outlook and entry of data into various systems/applications
  • Ability to perform all aspects of front office operations
  • Drive to achieve or exceed established service standards

Additional Data

  • 401(k) Retirement Plan with Employer Match
  • Medical, Vision, Prescription, Telehealth, & Dental Plans
  • Life & Disability Insurance
  • Paid Time Off & Extended Illness Days Offered
  • Colleague Referral Bonus Program
  • Tuition Reimbursement
  • Commuter Benefits
  • Dependent Care Spending Account
  • Employee Discounts

This position is eligible to earn a base compensation rate in the state range of $18.18 to $23.64 hourly depending on job-related factors as permitted by applicable law, such as level of experience, geographic location where the work is performed, and/or seniority.

  • External candidates: submit your application on concentra.com/careers

title: Women's Network Steering Group Member
description:
Are you passionate about creating a more inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive?

The Affinity Water Women's Network is looking for 4 new Steering Group members to help drive positive change across our business.

We are keen to build a Steering Group that reflects the diversity of women in our workforce. Whether you are early in your career, an experienced leader, or work in operations, field-based roles, customer teams or corporate functions, your voice matters. The broader the range of perspectives we bring together, the stronger and more representative our network will be.

Our network aims to create a supportive and inclusive community that empowers women, raises awareness of barriers to gender equality, and helps influence the policies, practices and culture that enable people from all backgrounds to succeed.

We also recognise the important role that allies play in creating an inclusive workplace for women, and we welcome applications from anyone who shares our commitment to gender equity.

Working alongside our Executive Sponsor, Liv Walton, and Network Co-Chairs, Jane McGoven and Emma Warren, Steering Group members will help to:

  • Champion the Women's Network across all Affinity Water sites and teams.

  • Increase support for women in operational and other roles where they are traditionally under-represented.

  • Promote inclusion, belonging and gender equity throughout the organisation.

  • Help identify and raise awareness of issues affecting attraction, retention, progression and representation of women.

  • Support events, campaigns and initiatives that celebrate diversity and encourage meaningful conversations, including engaging with other networks and the wider EDI community

  • Provide feedback and insights that help shape the company’s wider EDI priorities and activities.

  • Build connections and create opportunities for peer support and networking across the business.

You do not need previous EDI or committee experience to apply.

We are looking for diverse perspectives and lived experiences, commitment and enthusiasm about creating an inclusive workplace. We want people who are willing to share ideas and, committed to making a positive difference.

You will be expected to be a role model for inclusion and dignity and respect at work.

Steering group responsibilities are likely to require, a minimum of 1-2 hours a month (it’s a good idea to speak with your line manager about the time commitment and how you will accommodate this before applying).

What's in it for you?

As a Steering Group member, you'll:

  • Attend monthly steering group meetings.

  • Work closely with other steering group members, including our co-chairs and Executive Sponsor.

  • Build your professional network across Affinity Water.

  • Develop skills in leadership, collaboration, influencing, event planning and stakeholder engagement.

  • Contribute to meaningful change that positively impacts colleagues across the organisation.

  • Build confidence, visibility and experience that can support your future career development.

  • This is your opportunity to help shape the future of the Women's Network and influence how Affinity Water continues to build an inclusive culture where everyone can thrive.

Employee networks play a vital role in helping us foster a culture of inclusion, improve understanding of different experiences and drive meaningful change. By joining the Steering Group, you can help shape the future of the Women’s Network and support an inclusive culture where everyone can thrive and achieve their potential. For more information about our EDI strategy and how our networks fit in: Our employee networks.pptx.

If you'd like to help create positive change, build your network, develop new skills and be part of something meaningful, we'd love to hear from you. Complete the short application form on TeamTailor and tell us why you'd like to join the Women's Network Steering Group.

We look forward to hearing from you.

Emma & Jane
